TITLE: 2Box
LVL_SEED_REBUILD: Rebuild the level from its seed
HINT_NONE: No moves left — reset the level
HINT_WAIT: Both boxes are trapped — skip a move with any direction
HELP_GOAL: Two boxes, two pads. Slide the coral box onto the coral pad and the gold box onto the gold pad. When both sit on their pads, the level is solved.
HELP_MOVE: One gesture moves both boxes: they slide the same way until they hit a wall, the edge of the field or each other. The second box often acts as a brake for the first — that is what most solutions are built on.
HELP_COMPASS: This is the game compass: W is west, S is south, N is north and E is east. The hint under the field shows the W and S axes, and the letters on the sides of the boxes repeat the same directions — they show how a box is turned. The level can be rotated: drag with the mouse or use two fingers to check the sides and look behind the boxes.
HELP_CELLS: Besides plain tiles the field has cells with mechanics. Every episode brings its own set:
HELP_CTRL_MOVE: Swipe on the field or use the arrow keys to make a move.
HELP_CTRL_ORBIT: Two fingers or mouse drag rotates the level around the vertical axis so you can look behind the boxes.
HELP_CTRL_UNDO: Undo takes back the previous move; reset starts the level over.
HELP_CTRL_HINT: The lightbulb button shows the first move of the shortest solution when one exists.
HELP_TIP: Stuck? Step back: many levels are solved by an unexpected first move. Hotkeys: R — reset, Esc — pause.
DEBUG_GENERATE_FAILED: Could not build a level with this set. Try another difficulty.
DEBUG_SEED_INVALID: The seed must be a number: decimal or 0x-hex.
MECH_PORTAL_DESC: Entering sends the box to the paired exit.
MECH_TRAP_DESC: A box stops: the weak trap skips one move, the strong one skips two.
MECH_ROTATOR_DESC: An elbow turns a box only when it enters from the marked side; otherwise the box passes straight through.
MECH_GYRO_DESC: A cell always turns movement by 90°, from any side.
MECH_SWITCH_DESC: A button flips every elbow and gyro.
TUTORIAL_GOAL:
Each cube has its own pad: the coral one belongs on the coral pad, the gold one on the gold pad. Both cubes obey a single gesture: they slide the same way until a wall, the edge of the field or the other cube stops them. So the second cube always blocks the first — that is where the puzzles come from.

When both cubes stand on their pads, the level is done.
TUTORIAL_ORBIT_TITLE: Rotating the level and the compass
TUTORIAL_ORBIT:
The level can be rotated: drag with the mouse or use two fingers on the field. The field turns, not the cubes — moves work the same way, but you can see what hides what and where the pads are.

The compass under the field marks west (W) and south (S). Arrow keys move the cubes along the sides of the field, not the screen, so check the compass after turning. The letters on the cube faces are the same directions: they show how a cube ended up after a turn.
TUTORIAL_PORTAL:
A cube that enters a portal comes out of the paired one and keeps going in the same direction. If the other cube stands on the exit, the two trade places.

A portal does not skip a move: it carries a cube across the field while the other cube moves as usual. So solutions usually come down to choosing which cube to send through.
TUTORIAL_TRAP:
A cube that drives into a trap gets stuck: the weak one holds it for one move, the strong one for two. A stuck cube does not move and works like a wall — both for the other cube and as a stopper.

The move still counts while a cube sits in a trap: the other cube slides. The stuck one only frees itself when the trap lets go.
TUTORIAL_ROTATOR:
An elbow turns a cube 90°, but only when the cube enters from the entry side — every cell has its own, drawn on the tile. From other sides the elbow behaves like a plain tile and the cube drives straight through.

That is why one cell is sometimes a turn and sometimes a passage: it all depends on the direction you came from.
TUTORIAL_SWITCH:
The button flips every elbow and gyro on the field: right and left swap, and routes that worked before now lead the other way.

A cube that lands on the button flips the field for everyone — including on the way back.
TUTORIAL_ONEWAY:
A tile with an arrow lets a cube through only along that arrow: with the arrow it is a passage, against it a wall.

Because of that the way there can be shorter than the way back, and sometimes there is only one way in — choose which cube goes first.
